1. A pending non-Clifford frame can now be physically settled

The earlier native Bell instrument implements a gate with a recorded correction frame. The apparent difficulty was that, during classical decoding latency, identity refreshes keep creating newer Pauli frames. Waiting until the entire current frame is known therefore need not terminate.

That requirement is stronger than necessary.

Choose a fixed universal alphabet in the third Clifford hierarchy, such as  $H,S,\mathrm{CNOT},\mathrm{Toffoli}$ . For a bounded-arity gate  $G$ , combine its incoming Pauli frame and its Bell-measurement byproduct into a Pauli  $P$ . The accepted raw instrument has logical action

 $GP=C_G(P)G,
\qquad
C_G(P):=GPG^\dagger.$ Because  $G$  belongs to the third Clifford hierarchy,  $C_G(P)$  is a Clifford.

Call the records determining  $P$  the old prefix. During the time needed to decode and deliver that prefix, native identity refreshes add a newer Pauli  $Q$  on the left. The logical state therefore has the form

 $Q\,C_G(P)\,G|\psi\rangle.$ There is no independence assumption here:  $Q$ ,  $P$ , the other records, syndrome variables, and the untouched reference may be correlated.

Once the old prefix is known, execute a physical native  $C_G(P)^\dagger$ -Choi instrument. If that instrument contributes a fresh raw Pauli byproduct  $R$ , its output is

 $\begin{aligned}
C_G(P)^\dagger RQ\,C_G(P)\,G|\psi\rangle
&=P_{\mathrm{new}}G|\psi\rangle,\\
P_{\mathrm{new}}
&:=C_G(P)^\dagger RQ\,C_G(P).
\end{aligned}$ The new frame is Pauli because Clifford conjugation preserves the Pauli group.

Thus the old prefix determines the physical correction, while the newer unknown frame can remain unknown. The next non-Clifford operation on that logical dependency waits until this physical Clifford correction has occurred. No Clifford correction is concealed in a final decoder.

This is an operator identity on the logical system tensored with the identity on an arbitrary reference. Its noisy implementation uses the accepted complete native instrument, including its actual Davies evolution and faulty physical records.
